samples.name: (Abdominal part of pectoralis major muscle)
samples.text:
(ABDOMINAL PART OF PECTORALIS MAJOR)


The more frequent variations include greater or less extent of attachment to the ribs and sternum, varying size of the abdominal part or its absence, greater or less extent of separation of sternocostal and clavicular parts, fusion of clavicular part with deltoid, and decussation in front of the sternum. 



https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoralis_major

samples.name: (Adductor minimus)
samples.text:
(ADDUCTOR MINIMUS)


Small and flat skeletal muscle in the thigh which constitutes the upper, lateral part of the adductor magnus muscle. 

It adducts and laterally rotates the femur.

The adductor minimus originates on the pelvis at the inferior ramus of the pubis as the anterior-most part of the adductor magnus. 

It is inserted on the back of the femur at the medial lip of the linea aspera and thus crosses the proximal part of the true adductor magnus.


=== Innervation ===

    -obturator nerve
    -tibial nerve (L3-5), 
    -a branch of the sciatic nerve



https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adductor_minimus_muscle

samples.name: (Opponens digiti minimi muscle of foot)
samples.text:
(OPPONENS DIGITI MINIMI MUSCLE OF FOOT)


The Flexor digiti minimi brevis (Flexor brevis minimi digiti, Flexor digiti quinti brevis) lies under the metatarsal bone on the little toe, and resembles one of the Interossei.

It arises from the base of the fifth metatarsal bone, and from the sheath of the Fibularis longus; its tendon is inserted into the lateral side of the base of the first phalanx of the fifth toe.

Occasionally a few of the deeper fibers are inserted into the lateral part of the distal half of the fifth metatarsal bone; these are described by some as a distinct muscle, the opponens digiti quinti. 



https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flexor_digiti_minimi_brevis_muscle_of_foot

samples.name: (Third trochanter)
samples.text:
(THIRD TROCHANTER)


In human anatomy, the third trochanter is a bony projection occasionally present on the proximal femur near the superior border of the gluteal tuberosity. 

When present, it is oblong, rounded, or conical in shape and sometimes continuous with the gluteal ridge. 

Structures analogous to the third trochanter are present in other mammals, including some primates.

It is called the third trochanter in reference to the greater and lesser trochanters that are always present on the femur.

Its function is to provide an attachment for the ascending tendon of the gluteus maximus muscle. 



https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_trochanter
